messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
I’d add that I want a fair financial share, but I haven’t set a price. I’m not in a rush; I just don’t want to subsidize A’s purchase.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but we haven’t settled on a price or terms. C’s agreement matters, and I know she hasn’t agreed.
Thank you. I don’t have a particular plan for the house yet. I would like some money from the estate to start a dance studio, though I’m not sure what amount or share would be fair.
Yes, I’m open to an independent appraisal as a starting point. It wouldn’t settle whether we can agree on a family discount, though.
Yes, an independent appraisal and confirmation of the shares sound sensible. I don’t yet know how much the studio would need or when—I’d have to work that out.
I’m open to an independent appraisal and checking the will, but I’m not agreeing to a sale yet. We need to know the estate shares and discuss the terms first.

I don’t have a specific discount in mind yet. I’d like a price my husband and I can manage, while being fair to B and C. Let’s see the appraisal and confirmed shares first; I’m open to discussing payment over time too.
I don’t know who the executor or estate lawyer is. The executor should arrange the appraisal if one has been appointed; otherwise, we should agree who will handle it.
Yes, I can work on a rough budget and timeline. I can’t give you figures just yet, but I’ll try to have something more concrete once I’ve looked into the costs.
I’m not sure who the executor is or which lawyer has the will.
I’m not sure who the executor is or which lawyer holds the will. I’ll check what I can.
That sounds like a sensible next step. I’ll check Dad’s papers and contact his past lawyer if I can identify them.
